patch_description: Radically cuts parameter count to a single shared angle "theta" reused across every gate in the block (one global RY layer, one final global RZ layer, and three entangling shells at graph-distances 1, 2, and 4 on the 8-qubit ring). Crucially, instead of tying multiple gates of the *same* generator (which is nearly redundant), each entangling shell uses a *different* two-qubit generator (CRZ, CRX, CRY respectively) so that, even though the scalar angle is shared, the resulting one-parameter family of unitaries explores non-commuting directions of the Lie algebra — preserving much of the expressive entangling structure that gave the previous 2-parameter design good worst-group margins, while only paying for one trainable circuit parameter (theta) plus the fixed gain/bias. This directly targets the dominant scoring lever (parameter economy) with no loss of circuit depth or shell connectivity (still 3 shells spanning the whole ring with short paths between any two qubits), and should also converge faster and generalize better on the tiny training set since there is only one angle to fit.
